- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.18) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to avoid overbought overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.36) and price is trending up, model frequently underestimates continuation; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 periods to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.18–0.36) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 3-period moving average correction to smooth out erratic forecasts.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate true price at end of period; add 1–3% buffer to final forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.09) and price is falling, model often underpredicts depth of decline; extend downward slope by 1–2% per period to reflect bearish sentiment persistence.
